attempted_claim: Let u ∈ C(I;Ḣ¹(ℝ⁴)) be a radial maximal-lifespan solution on I = (−T₋, T₊) of i∂ₜu + Δu + |u|²u = 0, with E(u) = ½∫ℝ⁴|∇u|² dx − ¼∫ℝ⁴|u|⁴ dx = E(W), ||∇u(0)||₂ > ||∇W||₂, and W(x) = (1 + |x|²/8)⁻¹. If T₊ = +∞ or T₋ = +∞, must u equal the Duyckaerts–Merle special solution W⁺ up to phase, scaling, space/time translation, and time-reversal/conjugation symmetries? Here W⁺ is the threshold solution with E(W⁺) = E(W), supercritical kinetic norm, and W⁺(t) → W in Ḣ¹ as t → +∞.
decisive_failure: The investigation attempted concentration-compactness, modulation/ejection, and truncated-virial routes but could not supply the uniform mass-free virial control needed for global rigidity; the corrected scaling computation covers only fixed profiles, and no complete or original alternative result was established within the pass.
